concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 2 / research.md Methodology §2 / data-model.md Composition Graph
concerns.text: The composition graph encodes NO stoichiometry. Nodes are unique elements with fixed periodic-table features; edges are fully-connected with weights = fixed pairwise property distances. The graph for FeO and Fe2O3 (or any two compounds sharing an element set) is IDENTICAL, so the GNN input is invariant to element ratios. The model cannot learn composition-dependent band gap/hardness; construct validity of the entire representation is broken. Add composition fractions (e.g., node feature = element fraction, or edge weight scaled by co-occurrence) — pymatgen Composition provides this directly.

With no verified dataset, the plan cannot answer the research question at all — it delivers a tested pipeline but zero scientific evidence. The plan is transparent about this, which is correct, but the methodology as planned yields no results for SC-001/SC-005/SC-006 either, not just SC-002. This must be resolved (verified dataset or scope revision) before the plan can be accepted as a methodology for answering the question.

Power claim 'detecting ΔR² ≈ 0.05 between dependent models is well-powered (power > 0.80 at α = 0.05, Cohen 1988 conventions)' is unsupported: Cohen's conventions are for standardized mean differences, not differences in R² between correlated CV folds, and no test (e.g., paired comparison across folds, corrected resampled t-test) is named. State the actual comparison procedure or soften the claim; also note 5 folds gives only 5 paired observations, which is itself weakly powered.

The '95% prediction intervals as mean ± 1.96 × std of fold predictions' conflates prediction uncertainty with fold-variance of point estimates; with 5 folds the ±1.96×std interval has poor coverage. Acceptable as a spec-mandated convention (FR-007), but the report should label it as a fold-disagreement interval, not a calibrated 95% PI.

FR-005/FR-011 (structure-aware graph from MP CIFs) and SC-002 (ΔR² information loss) have NO executable plan element — Phase 8 delivers only a 'code path only' stub with no scientific run, and the plan itself declares 'SC-002 is not computable'. The spec is the root cause: it assumes MP Open Data + ungated CIF API, which the plan reports as unavailable/credential-gated. This needs a spec revision (kickback to clarified): either re-scope FR-005/FR-011/SC-002 to a verifiable open CIF source, or remove them and amend constitution Principle VI, which currently REQUIRES the structure-aware comparison for every reported metric.

FR-006's explicit ΔR²/ΔMAE/ΔRMSE computation 'on the shared test set' and US-2's `results_structure_aware.json` / `comparison_summary.csv` deliverables are unbacked — the plan substitutes an RF-baseline gap explicitly labeled 'NOT a structure information-loss metric'. The spec still mandates these outputs; either the spec must be revised to match the reduced scope or a verified data path must be restored.

US-1 scenario 2 (inference on a NEW chemical formula returning predicted band gap/hardness with a timestamp and 95% CI) has no plan element: no inference CLI/script exists in the project structure or phases; Phase 6 computes fold-level prediction intervals on test data only. Add an inference entry point or revise the spec scenario.

concerns.location: spec.md:Assumptions (1.5 × IQR outlier rule); spec.md:FR-006 'shared test set'
concerns.text: The spec's assumed 1.5×IQR outlier cleaning is absent from the plan's Phase 1 ingestion (drop-and-warn on missing values only) — either add it or note the deviation. Also FR-006 specifies metrics on a shared held-out test set while the plan reports 5-fold CV means; the plan should state this deviation explicitly in its FR-006 mapping.

concerns.location: plan.md:Constitution Check / Limitations; spec.md:FR-005, FR-006, FR-011, SC-002
concerns.text: The plan explicitly cannot deliver FR-005/FR-006(structure portion)/FR-011 or compute SC-002, and states 'scope revision required' — yet the spec remains unchanged and the plan proceeds to task generation. Plan and spec are mutually incompatible as written; the plan should either trigger a spec revision (amending FR-005/FR-011/SC-002 or the constitution Principle VI) before tasks, or the plan's Constitution Check should not proceed on an unamended spec. Downstream tasks will reference FRs the plan itself declares unimplementable.

Principle I is marked PASS ('dataset loader reads from a single canonical, contract-validated source; every run re-downloads/validates the same file'), but the plan's own Summary and Limitations state no verified dataset exists and quickstart.md requires the user to manually 'Place a CSV/parquet' at data/raw/materials.csv. There is no canonical source to re-download; the PASS claim contradicts the blocking finding two paragraphs above. Mark it PARTIAL/flagged like Principle VI.

Phase 8 promises a structure graph builder 'implemented and unit-tested on a bundled 2-line CIF fixture', but the Project Structure tree lists only src/graphs/composition.py and tests/fixtures/tiny_materials.csv — no structure-graph module, no CIF-fetch wrapper module, and no CIF fixture file. The Phase 8 deliverable has no home in the declared structure; add the files (e.g. src/graphs/structure.py, src/data/cif_fetch.py, tests/fixtures/tiny.cif).

concerns.location: data-model.md vs spec.md US-2 / plan.md Phase 6
concerns.text: Spec US-2 acceptance scenarios name results_structure_aware.json and comparison_summary.csv; data-model.md and the metrics contract define neither (consistent with the omission), but plan Phase 6 emits 'Δmetrics vs RF baseline clearly labeled as a baseline gap' with no defined artifact for that delta block. The model_metrics.schema.yaml rf_baseline description covers the labeling, but the plan should state explicitly which artifact carries the delta so Principle IV (SSoT) traceability holds.

The project's primary scientific contribution (Constitution Principle VI: ΔR² information loss, SC-002) and the entire scientific training/evaluation run are not executable — no verified dataset with formula/band_gap/hardness/crystal_system exists and the structure-aware baseline is unavailable. The plan honestly flags this, but as planned it can only deliver a tested pipeline with zero scientific results; the research question cannot be answered. This requires scope revision (new verified dataset or reframed question) before the plan is scientifically sound, not just a limitation note.

Interpretability validation is quasi-circular: PCs are correlated with 'atomic mass, melting point, bulk modulus'. Atomic mass is essentially a monotone function of atomic number, an input node feature — a significant correlation is near-guaranteed by construction, not evidence of meaningful learning. Bulk modulus is physically the basis of the hardness training target, so correlating embeddings with it is close to validating against the label. Choose genuinely held-out properties (e.g., thermal conductivity, sound velocity) or drop atomic mass.

The composition 'graph' is fully-connected with edge weights computed as Euclidean distance in the SAME 4-D property space used for node features. The graph therefore carries no information beyond the node features (it is a deterministic function of them), and standard GCNConv ignores edge_weight unless explicitly wired. The GNN-vs-RF comparison is still valid, but the plan should acknowledge the graph adds no compositional information (e.g., stoichiometry is only weakly encoded via pooling) — otherwise the 'graph representation' framing overstates what is tested.

'95% prediction intervals as mean ± 1.96 × std of fold predictions' is not a prediction interval for a new material — fold-to-fold model variance does not capture residual/aleatoric error, so the interval will be far too narrow. Either rename it a fold-uncertainty band or compute a proper prediction interval (e.g., conformal or residual-based).

The claim 'detecting ΔR² ≈ 0.05 ... power > 0.80 at α = 0.05, Cohen 1988 conventions' is asserted without a test, effect-size metric, or dependence structure (paired folds). Either state the power analysis will be computed at run time with the actual fold-level ΔR² values (e.g., paired t-test across folds) or remove the numeric claim.
